title: Knife gate valve on thickener underflow, passing when closed
tests: Natural deterioration; root with no action; isolation safety.
summary: A knife gate valve on the thickener underflow line passed slurry when closed, so the line could not be isolated for maintenance. The elastomer sleeve was worn at normal rate (about 14 months). The tree has the root cause but no action against it.

problem.title: Knife gate valve V-2210 passing when closed on thickener underflow
problem.site: Iron ore processing plant, Pilbara WA
problem.whatHappened: V-2210 was closed on 30 Jan 2026 to isolate the line for a pump job. Slurry kept passing the gate and flowed to the open pipe. The job was stopped and the line was isolated further upstream by draining the thickener. The elastomer sleeve was worn and cut at the bottom of the gate seat.
problem.where: Bottom of the elastomer sleeve and gate seat on V-2210.
problem.when: During a planned pump job. Valve last serviced about 14 months earlier.
problem.impact: Planned job delayed 8 hours, thickener drained, slurry spill to the bund. No injury.
problem.makeModel: 300 mm knife gate valve, elastomer sleeve, pneumatic actuator
problem.duty: Isolates thickener underflow line to the pump, slurry about 55% solids

evidence.title: Worn sleeve and gate seat
evidence.note: Sleeve cut and thin at the bottom 20% of the seat. Gate blade polished, no gouging.

evidence.title: Valve service history
evidence.note: Sleeve changed at 14, 13 and 15 months on the last three occasions. Same duty.

evidence.title: Stores catalogue
evidence.note: No sleeve kit for this valve size held in stores.

mustSuggest.idea: No planned sleeve change based on the 13 to 15 month history
No isolation proving step in the permit or job procedure for slurry lines
No spare sleeve and no min/max in stores
Valve passing was only found when the job started because there is no inspection of valve sealing

acceptable: Valve operated partially open causing wear

mustFlag.note: Physical root, no system cause beneath it besides the stores node which is not linked to it

challenge.expectation: Summary says the tree is clear and evidenced but has only a repair action; asks about interval, spare and isolation proving.
deliberateWeaknesses: Root n2 has no preventive action at all (no_preventive)
n3 spares gap not flagged as a root, no action
No condition monitoring of isolation integrity before a job
Isolation safety method: no one proves the isolation before work starts

capa.deteriorationReasoning: Sleeve lives of 13 to 15 months in abrasive slurry are consistent: normal wear to be managed by an interval, monitoring and a spare.

preventive.what: Replace elastomer sleeve before the shortest recent life
preventive.interval: starting point about 12 months, check against the site history and valve maker

preventive.what: Valve closed test (leak check across the gate) before any isolation use, and a periodic check
Hold 1 sleeve kit for this valve size and any matching valves
Isolation procedure for slurry lines requires proving the isolation by draining or a second barrier
Min/max in stores set from the interval

capa.spares: 1 sleeve kit per valve size in use; 21 day lead time, so min 1.
capa.rollout: All knife gate valves used for isolation on slurry: add the sleeve interval and a leak check.
unacceptable: Find the forcing cause as the main action
